newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian finance minister's resignation accepted.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian finance minister's resignation accepted.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius on Friday accepted the resignation of Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas, who said last week he wanted to quit because of a scandal over a bank loan.
"Prime Minister Vagnorius today accepted the resignation of Finance Minister Matiliauskas and will provide the draft decree to the president on Monday," the government office said in a statement.
Matiliauskas, 29, handed his resignation to Vagnorius on January 24 in the wake of allegations that he took a soft loan from a commercial bank where he once worked and which later went bankrupt.
Vagnorius asked the prosecutor's office to investigate whether Matiliauskas had done anything illegal by taking a loan on favourable terms from Kredito Bankas, a commercial bank.

The government office said in a statement the prosecutor's office found no wrongdoing over the credit. But it said investigators now were looking into other possible violations by Matiliauskas and would report in a month.

"Prime Minister Vagnorius thinks that neither society nor legislative bodies would be interested in Matiliauskas if he was a normal citizen who like hundreds of other bank employees received a soft credit," the statement said.
"But the responsibilities of high-ranking public servants are much tougher," it added.

Matiliauskas denied he did anything wrong while working at the bank and said he passed the loan on to one of the bank's owners. He also pointed out that he did not appear among the list of the bank's debtors when it went bankrupt.
Matiliauskas was the youngest member of Vagnorius' right-of-centre government, which swept former communists out of power last November.
He had not had time to make his mark at the finance ministry although he persuaded credit rating agency IBCA to give Lithuania a higher rating than that of another agency Moody's.
